$comment: Resolved content baselines for the federated entries in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
Deliberately NOT stored in marketplace.json: that file is consumed by Claude Code
against its own marketplace schema, and must not carry keys the plugin loader does
not expect. This sidecar is read only by scripts/check-federated-content.mjs.
Why it exists: a federated entry pins a tag by NAME, and a tag name is mutable.
Re-pointing it at different content is silent - every consumer follows, and the
existing pin check still passes because it only asks whether the tag resolves and
declares the matching version. lore-cli and quest-cli both had v0.6.0 deleted and
recreated on 2026-09-10/11 (OMARK-43); the skill content happened to be unchanged,
but nothing in CI could have told us if it had not been.
To update: re-resolve the chain yourself (tag ref -> tag object -> commit -> root
tree -> skills subtree), confirm the content is what you intend to ship, and record
the new SHA here in the same change that moves the pin. Updating this file is the
act of saying 'I verified this content', so do not update it to make CI go green.
Release handshake, agreed with the lore-cli session and tracked there as LCLI-469:
lore-cli messages this repository at tag-cut time with the tag name, the tag object
SHA, the commit it peels to, and the resolved skills/ tree SHA, so a new release
arrives with its baseline rather than as a red check here. The same is expected of
quest-cli. Do not take those SHAs on trust - they are a head start, not a
verification; re-resolve them here before recording, which is the whole point of
this file. If a pin bump ever lands without its baseline moving, the checker fails
on purpose rather than silently checking the wrong tag.

opum-lore.note: OMARK-78, dispatched by opum-agent (2026-09-30, go for the LCLI-469 handshake bump) as a paired lore+quest 0.12.0 bump (Opum constitution Article 3 clause 4: both pins move to the same version in one change). Zero content change on this entry: skills/ at v0.12.0 is byte-identical to the v0.11.0 baseline -- same subtree SHA ce580cd1..., proven by `git diff --quiet v0.11.0 v0.12.0 -- skills/` exiting 0, not an absent-diff heuristic. Chain re-resolved independently at bump time, never reused from the tag-cut handshake: local blobless fetch walked with rev-parse -- tag ref v0.12.0 -> tag object 070085b0e448340cb6f5a2156bc0a3a39399001d (type=tag) -> peels to commit 739f2b48e7f6d52a27c3d1a298ea4545ef2e7bf9 (also lore main, confirmed via `git ls-remote`) -> root tree 8d512d5c366715a70f43ca7df3265a50b04aec8f -> skills subtree ce580cd17d1da6a61ddb53f649398719b9262f96 -- cross-checked via `git ls-remote --tags` and via the GitHub API chain (git/ref/tags -> git/tags -> git/commits -> git/trees), the exact path check-federated-content.mjs walks. The tag was re-cut once during this cycle (first cut 2e726167 -> 57879cc8, superseded); every number above was resolved after the re-cut. .claude-plugin/plugin.json at the tag self-declares version 0.12.0, confirmed by direct read of the tagged commit. npm dist-tags.latest confirmed independently as 0.12.0 on the root launcher and all 6 platform packages; the launcher's release-candidate is 0.12.0-rc.1 (clause 5's staged-publish shape). No npm provenance attestation on the root launcher: its dist object carries no attestations key (`npm view @opum-ai/lore@0.12.0 dist --json`), against a positive control showing that key on attested packages (sigstore, @sveltejs/kit, pnpm, @octokit/core), so a measured absence rather than a null read; the condition is known and being recorded in lore-cli's own release-truth document. Cross-corroborated by opum-cli-e2e's pair receipt (origin/main 40fe8598fad663ca0918efa8417f54d743efc2a3, receipts/pair/0.12.0.json): pair.lore.commit 739f2b48 matches exactly, verdict QUALIFIED, 487 pass / 0 fail / 2 routine-blocked (unbound-scale plus a lore launcher byte-identity row whose post-move re-run result is tracked with the orchestrator before this change merges).

proof-skills.note: OMARK-73, dispatched by opum-agent (OPAG-437, operator ruling 2026-09-25: MIT-license and publish proof-skills under Opum AI). First pin of a fourth, non-federated-by-history plugin -- proof-skills is a new public repo, not a spin-off of an existing pin. Layout question (a git-subdir source into plugins/proof-skills/ vs. repo-root) was measured against this repository's own check-federated-pins.mjs, check-federated-content.mjs, and generate-codex-marketplace.mjs: none handle git-subdir without a code change (classifyEntry hardcodes source==='github'; resolveSubtree only walks one level into the root tree; generate-codex-marketplace.mjs's own test already locks in 'throw on git-subdir'), and Codex's per-plugin source has no documented subdirectory field. opum-agent ruled repo-root. v0.1.0 (the plugins/proof-skills/ subdir layout) shipped and stays published, unpinned here, and is never re-cut -- re-pointing it would be the exact tag-mutation shape OMARK-43 exists to catch. v0.1.1 ships the layout moved to the repo root instead, as a new tag. Tag chain resolved independently via the GitHub API and cross-checked via git ls-remote --tags (not taken from opum-agent's relay): v0.1.1 is an ANNOTATED tag -> tag object eb96f9681363f34d369612059814e17a300afd8f -> peels to commit 578749fd8baa6456d89d7a0037c88bc09a89213d, which is also the repository's main HEAD (confirmed via git/ref/heads/main) -> root tree 9a53258d828aee4b8d474b6428f8dc0fbf9661d5, carrying .claude-plugin/ and skills/ directly at the root (no plugins/ subdirectory) -> skills subtree 24b1cbc1685248b1a3b2a30ffb2b854a43efd050, containing formal-verify, lean-model, proof-simplify, and tlaplus-model. .claude-plugin/plugin.json at the tag self-declares name proof-skills, version 0.1.1, author {name: Opum AI, url: https://github.com/opum-ai}, license MIT -- confirmed by direct GitHub API contents read, matching what opum-agent relayed. Repository confirmed public (private: false) via the repos API, and MIT confirmed independently via the /license endpoint (spdx_id MIT).
